purpose: Nearest original methods for token-graph lead; bounded three-paper coverage

records.scope: Identity; Section2 magnetic Laplacian construction; Section3.1 complex spectral filtering

facts.finding: Directed edges enter phases of a complex Hermitian adjacency and magnetic Laplacian. The displayed construction uses nonnegative real Laplacian eigenvalues.
Complex graph convolution is a spectral filter; polynomial/Chebyshev realization avoids explicit diagonalization and learns filter coefficients.

interpretations: Our exp(-i tau H) is a special analytic Hermitian spectral filter, so complex graph propagation alone is not a new primitive.
records.difference: Our graph is built from per-example token-state overlaps and transports query amplitudes before Born readout. MagNet encodes input directed graph structure in a magnetic Laplacian and learns graph feature filters.
limits: Appendix proofs and code not inspected
No claim that the mechanisms are equivalent or that this paper exhausts the neighborhood

records.scope: Identity; coined-walk definition; neural forward algorithm; stated learning relaxation and experiment setup

facts.finding: Coin and shift operators propagate walk amplitudes; the network learns initial superpositions and/or coins.
The forward algorithm squares real amplitude entries and sums spin states to obtain a diffusion matrix, then applies it to input features. Learned coins relax unitarity and edge permutation symmetry.
The reported task is daily temperature prediction on a 409-location nearest-neighbor graph. This is a source description, not a replicated result.

interpretations: Amplitude propagation followed by squaring and feature diffusion is already present in a 2018 neural graph method.
records.difference: Current proposal uses class-query-dependent initial amplitudes, a fixed continuous unitary of a cubic-Gram token graph and the existing utility readout. The paper uses coined steps and learned initial amplitudes/coins; its learned version is not constrained to unitary coins.

records.scope: Identity; phase-aware attention equations and exact factorization; stated model/setup boundary

facts.finding: The compatibility score sums amplitude products multiplied by cosines of query/key phase differences, then uses the existing softmax attention pipeline.
An exact trigonometric factorization evaluates the score through two real matrix products, using amplitude-times-cosine and amplitude-times-sine features.
The paper describes a narrow attention substitution in a GPT-style controlled setting. We have not assessed its results or fairness.

interpretations: Concatenating the cosine and sine feature maps gives an ordinary real dot-product representation in a doubled feature dimension; this follows directly from Eqs4-5.
records.difference: The current proposal mixes amplitudes across token positions through U before squaring. Q-Interference changes pairwise compatibility through phase-aware feature maps and preserves softmax; these are structurally different operations.
limits: Results, appendicesB2-B4 and source code not inspected
